page: Microsoft Azure FX32-16mds_v2 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a dedicated clock speed of 4.2 GHz. It features 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The server is equipped with 672.0 GB of system memory, providing a high resource density of 42.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 1890 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2315.0 and a text processing score of 2959.0, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory write bandwidth for large uncached blocks is strong at 91.91 GB/sec, placing in the top 25%. Single-threaded operations also show strong performance, with gzip compression reaching 34.78 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.22 GB/sec. Multi-core performance, database operations, and Redis SET operations fall within the average middle 50% range.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the FX32-16mds_v2 offers a highly specialized hardware profile, trading a lower core count for massive memory capacity and high single-core clock speeds. This makes it a resource-dense option for workloads that are memory-bound rather than highly parallelized. The primary tradeoff is the moderate multi-core scaling, as reflected in the average multi-core benchmark scores. This server is suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale caching layers, text processing pipelines, and applications requiring high single-threaded CPU performance paired with large memory footprints.
